correctness.rationale: For the equicharacteristic local Gorenstein (1,2,1) ring, R=F_q ⊕V⊕F_q z with nondegenerate symmetric B:V×V→F_q; at nonzero u=c z, units and q−1 socle vertices split into q−1 stars K_(1,q³) plus isolated zero. The non-socle radical block is C⊗J_q with C_(v,w)=1[B(v,w)=c]. Solving two independent linear equations gives (C²)_(v,w)=q for v=w, 0 for distinct proportional, 1 for distinct lines. On projective-line constants, C=J−P for perp-involution P with exactly t isotropic fixed lines, giving eigenvalues q once, +1 (q+1−t)/2 and −1 (q−1+t)/2. On the line-zero-sum complement C²=qI and trace(C)−trace(C|H)=0, so equal ±sqrt(q) multiplicities. Combining all blocks yields X^(q^4−q²−2q+3)(X−q²)(X−q)^((q+1−t)/2)(X+q)^((q−1+t)/2)(X²−q³)^((q²+q−4)/2), rank q²+2q−3. Independent construction and diagonalization of full product matrices over q=2 and q=3 for each Witt type reproduced eigenvalue multiplicities. The general proof is combinatorial-algebraic and does not rely on finite diagonalization.

value.rationale: For a canonical intermediate nilpotence Gorenstein class omitted by the closest maximal/square-zero radical formulas, the natural multiplication-target matrix admits a complete uniform spectral classification for all prime powers, and its signed eigenvalue multiplicities recover the ring quadratic form’s Witt type. This is a motivated structural ring invariant, not a small unmotivated instance computation.
